macro.stance: Constructive on physical infrastructure, but maintain valuation discipline and a quality bias because the weekend did not add a new trading session and Friday's macro mix still combines resilient industrial demand with geopolitical oil risk and softer consumer data.
marketContext: No new U.S. cash-equity session occurred after Friday, August 14. The S&P 500 finished that session modestly lower while oil rose on renewed U.S.-Iran/Hormuz tension and weak retail/consumer data reduced the immediate case for a September Fed hike.

The strongest fresh weekend confirmation is supply-side: major manufacturers continue expanding data-centre power equipment capacity, reinforcing the idea that electrical and generation equipment remain bottlenecks rather than a one-quarter AI trade.

The cached Live Desk packet was generated on August 15, but Power/Grid, Nuclear, Uranium/Fuel, Oil & Gas and Metals theme states remained explicitly stale/neutral, so no conviction changes were driven by the overlay.

categoryReads.change: Strengthened bottleneck breadth; one new promotion
categoryReads.why: Fresh weekend reporting shows large manufacturers still expanding generator and electrical-equipment capacity for data centres. Powell Industries adds a smaller, more direct engineered-switchgear and power-distribution expression with record order momentum. Texas/PJM regulatory uncertainty still argues for equipment and behind-the-meter exposure over indiscriminate merchant-generation beta.
actions: Maintain GEV at the top of the equipment stack
Maintain ETN/HUBB/PWR as core T&D/electrical bottleneck exposures
Promote POWL at 8.2 as a priority switchgear/power-distribution research name
Keep CEG/VST/NRG/TLN on regulatory/grid-access watch rather than broadly downgrading them
